about: Every check in onefile-lint, with the evidence behind it. Grades describe the evidence, not how bad the failure is. Frequencies are quoted only where a source states them; everything else says so.

grades.A: measured on AI-generated pages or code, in a cited study or evaluation
grades.B: measured on the wider web, or named as a failure in a standard or official documentation

ms-eval.title: A11y LLM Eval report (Microsoft, GitHub Copilot SDK runs)
ms-eval.scope: 8 models, 32 prompt cases, 1280 control samples, run without accessibility instructions. [[CONFIRM: report generation date]]

suh-2025.title: Human or LLM? A Comparative Study on Accessible Code Generation Capability (Suh, Tafreshipour, Malek, Ahmed; arXiv, 20 Mar 2025)
suh-2025.scope: GPT-4o and Qwen2.5-Coder against human-written pages, scored with AChecker and QualWeb

a11yn.title: A11yn: Aligning LLMs for Web Accessibility-Aware UI Generation (Yoon et al.; arXiv 2510.13914, submitted 15 Oct 2025)
a11yn.scope: baseline Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct on the RealUIReq-300 benchmark; counts are average violations per the paper's Table 2

webaim-2026.title: The WebAIM Million, February 2026
webaim-2026.scope: 1,000,000 home pages; 95.9% had detected WCAG 2 failures. Human-made pages, not agent output

rules.title: No remote dependencies
rules.what: Scripts, stylesheets, fonts, frames, imports, images, audio, video and icons that load from another host, including CSS url() and @import, JavaScript import and import(), and import maps.
rules.why: A page that needs another host stops working offline, behind a firewall, or when that host changes or disappears. Scripts, stylesheets, fonts and frames are failures because the page breaks or changes; images, media and icons are warnings because it only degrades.
rules.how: Reads every URL in markup, inline CSS, style attributes and inline scripts. Anything starting with http(s):// or // counts. data:, blob: and #fragments do not. Use --allow-host to ignore hosts you accept.
rules.limits: Sees only URLs written out as text. Scripts that build a URL at run time are not seen. Links (<a href>) are not dependencies and are ignored.

evidence.finding: Simon Willison, 10 Dec 2025, describes loading libraries from a CDN as a standard pattern for single-file tools built with LLMs, so remote dependencies are common by design, not by accident.
Simon Willison, 9 Jul 2024: Claude Artifacts can load most code that is available via cdnjs, so pages made there usually carry CDN URLs.

rules.title: No sibling files
rules.what: Relative references (style.css, ./app.js, images/logo.png, /favicon.ico) in the same places remote-dependency reads.
rules.why: A page that points at files next to it is not one file. Email it, paste it into a chat or drop it into a gist and those references break.
rules.how: Same scan as remote-dependency. Any URL that is not remote, not data:/blob:/# is treated as a file next to the page.
rules.limits: A page that is meant to be served from a site with its own /favicon.ico will warn. That is a choice; skip the rule with --skip sibling-file.

evidence.finding: No public measurement found of how often agent output leaves sibling-file references. [[CONFIRM: frequency in agent-made pages]]

rules.title: Size
rules.what: File size in bytes and gzipped, the split between script, style and embedded data URIs, and a warning when base64 data takes over the file.
rules.why: A single file has to be downloaded, pasted or attached whole. Base64 is about a third larger than the bytes it encodes.
rules.how: Warns above 1024 KB and fails above 5120 KB by default. Change with --warn-kb and --fail-kb. Those limits are this tool's defaults, not a standard.
rules.limits: Size is reported for the decoded text of the file. The limits are a judgment call and depend on where the page will travel.

evidence.finding: No source found that sets a sensible size budget for a single-file page. The defaults are the author's choice. [[CONFIRM: a sourced budget]]

rules.title: Works offline
rules.what: Network calls in the page's own code: fetch, XMLHttpRequest, WebSocket, EventSource, sendBeacon, service worker registration, absolute form actions, and a linked web app manifest.
rules.why: Commenters in the Bento discussion on Hacker News singled out offline use. A service worker cannot help a single file: it must be a separate script and runs only over HTTPS or on localhost.
rules.how: Reads inline scripts for calls whose URL is a string literal.
rules.limits: Calls to a URL built at run time are not seen. A page that calls an API on purpose will warn; that is information, not a bug.

evidence.finding: Commenters on the Bento thread (1,033 points, 22 Jul 2026) singled out offline use as the standout feature of a one-file page.
MDN: service workers are restricted to HTTPS (localhost is allowed for development) and are registered from a separate script file.

rules.title: Print styles
rules.what: Whether the page has any @media print or @page rules, and two cases where having none does damage: a dark background, and a page root with overflow hidden or height 100vh.
rules.why: Pages made to be shared get printed or saved as PDF. MDN notes that browsers may leave backgrounds out of print, which can leave light text on white paper.
rules.how: Looks for @media print, @page and a print stylesheet link. Skips pages with almost no text.
rules.limits: Pages whose content is drawn by script after load can look empty to a static check and are skipped. The check does not render the page.

evidence.finding: MDN, print-color-adjust: a browser may leave out background images and adjust text colours when printing to suit white paper.
The Bento author said PDF printing works well in Chrome, which shows printing is part of how one-file decks are used.

rules.title: Document basics
rules.what: A doctype, a <meta charset> in the first 1024 bytes, a viewport meta tag, a lang attribute on <html>, and a page title.
rules.why: A page opened from disk has no server sending its encoding, so the charset tag has to do that job. Without it, non-ASCII text can show garbled. Without a viewport tag phones render at desktop width.
rules.how: Text checks on the start of the file and the parsed tags. A missing charset is a failure only when the file contains non-ASCII text.
rules.limits: Checks presence, not whether the values are right.

evidence.finding: MDN: a <meta> that declares the character encoding must be entirely within the first 1024 bytes of the document.
WebAIM Million 2026: 13.5% of home pages were missing a document language.

rules.title: Text contrast
rules.what: Text and background colour pairs that fall under 4.5:1 (3:1 for large text), read from CSS in the same rule, for light and dark mode, with custom properties resolved.
rules.why: Low contrast was the most common or second most common failure in all three agent-output sources read, and it is the most common failure on the wider web.
rules.how: Resolves var() from :root, parses hex, rgb, hsl, oklab, oklch and common colour names, and computes the WCAG 2 ratio. A colour with no background in its rule is checked against the page background and shown only as a note.
rules.limits: Reads CSS text, not computed styles. Gradients, images, color-mix(), lab() and currentcolor are skipped, never guessed. Text on a card is not compared with the page behind the card. Tools that render the page will find more. Skip with --skip contrast.

evidence.finding: A11y LLM Eval: colour contrast was 89.1% of axe failures across all models and cases.
Suh et al. 2025: contrast issues were 80% of all violations when scored with AChecker.
A11yn: colour contrast was the second most common violation for the baseline model, 702 on average.
WebAIM Million 2026: low-contrast text on 83.9% of home pages.

rules.title: Reduced motion
rules.what: Animation (CSS animation, @keyframes, movement transitions, smooth scrolling, autoplay video, requestAnimationFrame, Web Animations) with no prefers-reduced-motion query or check anywhere in the page.
rules.why: MDN names vestibular motion disorders as the reason people turn motion off.
rules.how: Counts motion sources and looks for the prefers-reduced-motion media query in CSS or a matchMedia check in script. Colour and opacity transitions are not counted.
rules.limits: Does not judge whether the reduced-motion path is good, only that one exists. A requestAnimationFrame loop may be a game or a chart, where the right answer differs.

evidence.finding: MDN: prefers-reduced-motion exists so pages can remove, reduce or replace motion; scaling or panning large objects can trigger vestibular discomfort.
No public measurement found of how often agent output ignores reduced motion. [[CONFIRM: frequency in agent-made pages]]

rules.title: Viewport height
rules.what: height: 100vh with no dvh or svh line in the same rule, overflow hidden on html or body, and a fixed pixel height on the page root.
rules.why: On phones 100vh is the height with the browser bar hidden, so a full-height block spills below the visible area. Overflow hidden on the page root makes anything below the fold unreachable and cuts printouts to one page.
rules.how: Reads height and overflow declarations in CSS rules.
rules.limits: Does not know whether a 100vh element is meant to overflow, such as a hero section. Treat as a prompt to look.

evidence.finding: web.dev, 29 Nov 2022: elements sized to 100vh bleed out of the viewport while browser toolbars are showing; svh, lvh and dvh units fix it.
No public measurement found of how often agent output uses 100vh. [[CONFIRM: frequency in agent-made pages]]

rules.title: Focus outline
rules.what: outline: none or 0 on a rule when nothing else in the page draws a focus indicator.
rules.why: Keyboard users lose track of where they are. W3C lists removing the focus indicator as a failure of success criterion 2.4.7.
rules.how: Finds outline removal, then looks for a :focus or :focus-visible style that draws something, or a replacement in the same rule.
rules.limits: A replacement set in script or a parent rule can be missed. The check is on CSS text.

evidence.finding: WCAG 2.4.7 Understanding: styling outlines so the focus indicator becomes non-visible is a listed failure (F78).
No public measurement found of how often agent output removes the focus ring. [[CONFIRM: frequency in agent-made pages]]

rules.title: Pinch zoom
rules.what: user-scalable=no or 0, or maximum-scale below 2, in the viewport meta tag.
rules.why: People who need larger text cannot zoom. The W3C test rule treats user-scalable=no and maximum-scale under 2 as failures.
rules.limits: Checks the tag only, not page-level scripts that intercept gestures.

evidence.finding: W3C ACT rule b4f0c3: fails if the viewport sets user-scalable to no or maximum-scale to less than 2; WCAG 1.4.4 asks for text resizing to 200%.

rules.title: Form labels
rules.what: Inputs, selects and textareas with no label for= link, wrapping label, aria-label, aria-labelledby or title. A placeholder alone is reported separately.
rules.why: A field with no programmatic label has no name for a screen reader, and a placeholder disappears as soon as someone types.
rules.how: Matches label for= to ids, walks up to a wrapping <label>, and checks the naming attributes.
rules.limits: A visible <label> that is not linked counts as unlabelled, which is correct but can surprise. Names set by script are not seen.

evidence.finding: A11y LLM Eval: form labels and required-field indicators failed in 5% to 70% of samples depending on the case; helper-text association failed in 50% to 100%.
WebAIM Million 2026: missing form input labels on 51% of home pages.

rules.title: Image alt text
rules.what: elements with no alt attribute at all. alt="" for decoration passes.
rules.why: Without alt, screen readers read the file name.
rules.how: Checks for the attribute, not its quality.
rules.limits: Does not judge whether alt text is useful, or whether an image of text should be real text.

evidence.finding: WebAIM Million 2026: missing alternative text on 53.1% of home pages.
Suh et al. 2025 found GPT-4o improved alternative text handling by over 70% against human code. Models do better here than elsewhere, so expect few hits from agent output.

rules.title: Button and link names
rules.what: Buttons and links with no text, aria-label, title, image alt or svg title.
rules.why: An icon-only button with no name is announced as just "button".
rules.how: Looks at text inside the element and the naming attributes of it and its children.
rules.limits: Icon fonts drawn with CSS content are invisible to this check and read as empty.

evidence.finding: A11yn: link-name was the fourth most common baseline violation, 129 on average.
WebAIM Million 2026: empty links on 46.3% and empty buttons on 30.6% of home pages.

rules.title: Tab order
rules.why: Positive values pull an element ahead of the natural tab order and usually break the reading sequence. W3C failure F44 covers tab orders that do not preserve meaning; positive tabindex is a common way to cause it.
rules.limits: A deliberate positive tabindex is rare but possible.

evidence.finding: WCAG 2.4.3 Understanding lists F44, using tabindex to create a tab order that does not preserve meaning and operability. The page does not name positive values specifically.
No public measurement found for agent output. [[CONFIRM: frequency in agent-made pages]]

rules.title: Keyboard-reachable clicks
rules.what: An inline onclick on an element that a keyboard cannot reach: no role and no tabindex, and not a button, link or form control.
rules.why: A div that acts as a button works with a mouse only. W3C lists emulating links this way as failure F42.
rules.limits: Listeners added with addEventListener cannot be matched to elements without running the page, so most modern code is not covered.

evidence.finding: WCAG 2.1.1 Understanding lists F42, a failure when static elements are made to act as links without keyboard support.
No public measurement found for agent output. [[CONFIRM: frequency in agent-made pages]]

rules.title: Main landmark
rules.what: A page with real text content and no <main> element or role="main".
rules.why: Screen reader users jump between landmarks. Missing landmarks were the most common baseline violation in one agent-output study and a large share of best-practice failures in another.
rules.how: Looks for <main> or role=main when the page has at least 200 characters of text.
rules.limits: Does not check the other landmarks (header, nav, footer) or that content sits inside them.

evidence.finding: A11yn: region (content outside landmarks) was the most common baseline violation, 894 on average, and landmark-one-main the third, 164.
A11y LLM Eval: landmark structure was 37% to 44% of best-practice failures.

not_checked.title: Modal dialog focus and keyboard behaviour

evidence.finding: A11y LLM Eval: modal dialog behaviour (hiding background content, focus management, keyboard trapping) failed in 52% to 92% of samples.

not_checked.why_not: Needs a browser that opens the dialog and presses Tab. A static check cannot tell.

not_checked.title: Skip navigation links

evidence.finding: A11y LLM Eval: skip navigation links were missing in all Shopping Home Page samples.

not_checked.why_not: Only matters on pages with repeated navigation, which is rare in one-file pages. Could be added as a check for pages with a <nav> and no skip link.

not_checked.title: ARIA attributes that are present but wrong

evidence.finding: Suh et al. 2025: models did worse than human developers on complex ARIA requirements, for example graphics labelling.

not_checked.why_not: Judging ARIA needs the accessibility tree, which needs a rendered page.
